more.title: Atomic magnetism reveals why iron, but not chromium, can produce ammonia using sunlight
more.summary: Two nearly identical materials have completely different chemical behavior. more.title: Macromolecular crowding could help build artificial cell systems
more.summary: Macromolecular crowding can serve as a design tool for controlling the formation and organization of synthetic DNA droplets, a study from Science Tokyo reveals. Researchers investigated this strategy using DNA nanostars and polymeric crowding agents to mimic the crowded cellular environment. They found that crowding promoted droplet formation and enabled control over droplet size, interactions and organization.

more.title: Molecular architecture determines tomato plant resistance to its main pest
more.summary: An international study investigating why wild tomatoes are more resistant to the tomato leafminer (Phthorimaea absoluta) than cultivated varieties revealed that the secret lies in the spatial structure of a plant defense molecule. The researchers mapped the biochemical origin of this difference and demonstrated that altering four amino acids in a single enzyme is sufficient to alter the structure of the substance…

more.title: Chornobyl dog population shows genetic signatures of directional selection
more.summary: The latest research on the wild population of dogs in Chornobyl reveals that the genetic differences between these dogs and other similarly isolated dog populations are likely evidence of directional selection, not mutation. The work suggests a potential association between genetic selection and environmental variables and could advance understanding of local adaptation and genomic resilience in contaminated…

more.title: Schools increasingly affected by poor air quality as wildfire smoke becomes more common
more.summary: American children are increasingly exposed to air pollution as wildfire smoke becomes more common, and some schools and child care centers struggle to keep indoor breathing conditions clean, a new national study shows.

more.title: Rarely seen deep-sea barreleye fish filmed in 4K
more.summary: During a recent expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard, MBARI scientists encountered a rarely seen barreleye fish (Macropinna microstoma). This sighting is MBARI's 11th observation of this unique deep-sea fish with a transparent head.

more.title: 150-year-old mystery about the identity of an 'extinct' giant crane solved
more.summary: Scientists at Bournemouth University (BU) have solved a 150-year-old mystery about the identity of an extinct giant crane that lived in Europe over 20,000 years ago. The work is published in the journal Royal Society Open Science.

more.title: Sun's outer magnetic field mapped in 3D for the first time
more.summary: A team of researchers has produced the first global, three-dimensional estimates of the sun's magnetic field, including the area beyond the sun's visible edge. This marks a step toward more accurate models of solar activity—and ultimately, better predictions of solar magnetic eruptions, which are the root cause of extreme space weather that can impact critical infrastructure technologies on Earth.

more.title: A new physics-informed AI tool aims to predict wildfire spread in real time and assist wildfire response
more.summary: A new AI system that NYU Fire Research Group describes as a digital twin of an active wildfire has, in early testing, shown the ability to forecast how a fire will spread in near real time.

more.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
more.author: Stephen Clark
more.summary: This Vulcan launch will be the first to utilize a full complement of six solid rocket boosters.

more.title: Exclusive: Numeracle Raises $28M To Keep Legitimate Business Calls From Spam Label
more.author: Judy Rider
more.summary: Numeracle, a McLean, Virginia-based company that verifies businesses and links their identities to the phone numbers they use to contact customers, has raised $28 million from Edison Partners to help businesses whose calls are incorrectly labeled as spam or blocked by phone carriers.

more.title: Humidity can change how smoke pollutants transform after dark
more.summary: What happens to smoke particles after sunset can depend strongly on something as familiar as the amount of water in the air. New research from Md. Sohel Rana and Marcelo I. Guzman at the University of Kentucky shows that relative humidity can redirect the chemical pathways involved in the nighttime oxidation of catechol, a phenolic compound associated with biomass burning.

more.title: How Spiders Spin ‘Silk Dope’ Into Nature’s Toughest Material
more.author: Yasemin Saplakoglu
more.summary: By probing its molecular structure, biologists are uncovering how a tangle of unstructured proteins turns into a tough, flexible thread. The post How Spiders Spin ‘Silk Dope’ Into Nature’s Toughest Material first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: Study finds celebrity digital twins may boost trust in customer service
more.summary: Imagine losing your credit card, logging into your bank's website for help and being greeted by a virtual customer service representative who looks and sounds exactly like actor Hugh Jackman. The person helping you isn't actually the Hollywood star—it's his AI-powered digital twin. And new research suggests that familiar face could significantly improve how you perceive your customer service experience.

more.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
more.author: Judy Rider
more.summary: Revenue growth does not guarantee a larger exit, as declining valuation multiples can outweigh operating gains and reduce enterprise value. Guest author Itay Sagie suggests that founders and boards should track valuation alongside financial performance, model the effects of delaying a sale, and begin M&A preparation while the business is strong and buyer interest is favorable.

more.title: Webb Sees Turbulent Star Nursery
more.author: HQ Web Team
more.summary: In this Webb image released on Oct. 22, 2026, we see a turbulent cauldron of star formation filled with dense clumps of gas. This region is named N159 and is located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This region has a lower metallicity […]

more.title: The DOE announces $5B loan to Constellation for nuclear uprates
more.author: Brian Martucci
more.summary: The pro-nuclear Trump administration continues to put its money where its mouth is. On Tuesday, the U.S. Department of Energy announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion to boost the output of 15 reactors at eight nuclear power plants in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania by a combined 1.1…

more.title: How childhood experiences shape employment outcomes in India
more.summary: Research led by the University of East Anglia (UEA) shows that childhood poverty, poor living conditions and gender can have lasting impacts on employment opportunities and earnings in India.

more.title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
more.author: Sufian Aldogom
more.summary: Modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results.

more.title: Optimistic climate futures for local communities in the UK imagined in a new report
more.summary: A new report co-authored by researchers from the University of York and WWF highlights how local communities across the U.K. imagine positive, sustainable, and resilient futures for the places where they live and work.
